data.why: No example channelmap files ship in the repo outside of test source code, so the NP24 (Neuropixels 2.0 four-shank) IMRO table used in tests/test_imro_io.py was reproduced verbatim as a real, parseable .imro file: seed/example-NP24.imro is placed at the repo root (the default channelmap directory) so it appears in the app's 'Input file' dropdown on launch, and an identical copy is kept in data/ as a reference artifact for the browser agent.

goals: load an existing Neuropixels channel map (.imro) and visualize electrode layout, density, and channel efficiency
create a new blank channel map for a chosen probe type (e.g. NP24) and build a blueprint by assigning electrode categories (full/half/quarter density, excluded, low priority)
interactively select electrodes with box/lasso tools and change their state (used/unused) or category to shape the recording configuration
run automatic electrode selection ('Refresh') to generate a valid channel map honoring per-channel hardware constraints from the current blueprint
save the finished channel map (.imro), its blueprint (.blueprint.npy), and view configuration for reuse or export
inspect electrode density/efficiency plots to judge whether the current selection meets experimental coverage goals before committing

review.summary: This tree captures what NeuroCarto is for: painting a density blueprint, letting the solver build a channel map within the hardware's channel budget, judging it by efficiency, density and conflicts, and saving the file bundle. All 11 screens I checked show what their nodes say. It needs small fixes before filing: state that Save requires a complete map, fix the reference-setting caveat, drop the interface-chore tasks, and record that the atlas view failed for a missing dependency, not because the app lacks it.
